title: Elis Regina's birth chart
metaDescription: Elis Regina's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 26.7° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 15.5° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 26.7° into Pisces — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Mars. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 11.8° Aries; Venus stands at 2.4° Taurus; Mars stands at 24.1° Aquarius. The tradition reads thought that arrives already in motion from Mercury, attraction that grows by reliability from Venus, effort aimed through strategy and words from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Uranus a sixth of the circle apart from Pluto, 1.3° off exact. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Saturn square Neptune at 1.3°, and Venus sextile Saturn at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Neptune while both square Saturn. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Moon in Taurus at 15.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Taurus at 2.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Virgo at 22.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Cancer at 4.0° is in detriment. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 earth, 3 air, 2 water, 2 fire by element and 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 3 cardinal by mode. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.6° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 15.5°.
